title: a gate rejection citing no DoD item is invalid and consumes no revision
proves: uncitedRejection in judge-gate.mjs treats a failing judge verdict on a node with a judgment item as a judge protocol failure when none of its findings names that item's id anywhere in their description or evidence — the judge's own turn is malformed, not the work. applyRejection is never reached for it: the first uncited rejection spends the node's one bounded judge re-ask (same runtime, same worker attempt, state.revisions untouched); a second uncited rejection has no re-ask left and blocks the node with error code judge_protocol, still without ever touching state.revisions, since a protocol failure in the judge's own output was never a verdict on the work to revise.

contract.goal: prove an uncited judge rejection is a protocol failure that spends no worker revision
